- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) and price drops, model underestimates; add 1–2% buffer to forecast for 5–7 days.
- Model frequently overpredicts mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if recent 7-day average is stable, forecast should align with 14-day moving average.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model exhibits high variance; use 10-day rolling median as anchor for 30-day forecast.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after 10–15 days, model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias of 1–2% per 3-day window.
- Sentiment spikes (≥0.8) correlate with model overconfidence; reduce forecast by 1–2% for 3–5 days after sentiment peak.
